claims.text: Catastrophic forgetting does not cause BERT fine-tuning instability.
Small fine-tuning dataset size inherently does not cause BERT fine-tuning instability.
Fine-tuning instability in transformer models like BERT, RoBERTa, and ALBERT is caused by optimization difficulties early in training that lead to vanishing gradients.
Performance variance across successful fine-tuning runs late in training is driven by differences in generalization performance despite near-equivalent training loss.
Catastrophic forgetting during failed fine-tuning runs is concentrated primarily in the top layers of the pre-trained transformer model.
Training on small datasets for the same number of total iterations as on full datasets recovers the original fine-tuning stability variance.
Fine-tuning BERT with Adam using bias correction and 20 training epochs achieves a performance standard deviation of 2.7 on RTE, 0.8 on MRPC, and 1.8 on CoLA across 25 random seeds.

evidence.description: Failed fine-tuning runs exhibit trivial training loss close to -ln(1/2) and accuracy matching majority baseline, indicating optimization failure rather than catastrophic forgetting learning.

Fine-tuning BERT on 1,000 sampled points from MRPC, CoLA, and QNLI for as many iterations as the full dataset almost completely recovers original fine-tuning accuracy variance and eliminates failed runs.
L2 gradient norm analysis shows failed runs suffer from vanishing gradients in bottom transformer layers throughout training, whereas successful runs exhibit growing gradients across all layers.
Across 450 fine-tuned BERT models on RTE, models achieving training loss as low as 10^-5 display significant spread in development set accuracy ranging from ~60% to over 75%.
Substituting pre-trained weights for the top 10 out of 24 layers in failed BERT runs recovers masked language modeling perplexity on WikiText-2 to pre-trained baseline levels.
Downsampled training for 1k points over 26 epochs on CoLA and 312 epochs on QNLI reduced run failures to match full dataset levels.
Table 1 shows proposed fine-tuning strategy reduces RTE std from 4.5 (Devlin) and 7.9 (Lee) to 2.7, MRPC std to 0.8, and CoLA std to 1.8 across 25 random seeds (p < 0.001 on Levene's test).

methodologies.name: Bias-corrected extended fine-tuning baseline
methodologies.description: Fine-tuning pre-trained transformer language models using AdamW with bias correction enabled, learning rate of 2e-5, and 20 training epochs with 10% linear warmup and decay.

limitations.text: Default fine-tuning practices omit Adam bias correction and use a fixed small epoch count (3 epochs), leading to early vanishing gradients and unstable training on small datasets.
Increasing the number of fine-tuning epochs increases the per-run computational cost, although it is recommended only for small datasets.
The analysis and recommendation to increase training epochs is primarily targeted at small datasets where iteration count is low.

future_work.text: Investigating fine-tuning instability and catastrophic forgetting in settings where supervised fine-tuning serves as an intermediate task training step for domain adaptation.
